purpose: Test exact rank-polynomial evaluation on a constructed family where a decomposable deterministic representation has an obvious linear factorization but an OBDD can be strongly order-sensitive. This is a representation-switch feasibility test, not an empirical claim about arbitrary formulas.
formula_family: For m independent pairs, F_m = AND_i (x_i iff y_i). Each pair is represented directly as deterministic smooth OR((not x_i AND not y_i),(x_i AND y_i)); pair modules are combined by decomposable AND.
exact_oracle: The rank polynomial is (1+z^2)^m, so coefficient at weight 2k is C(m,k) and odd coefficients are zero. Both direct decomposable circuit and every completed OBDD must match this vector exactly.

resource_guard.on_guard: mark guarded; do not interpolate missing size

predeclared_tests: All unguarded representations must match the exact closed-form rank vector.
Report scaling separately for direct decomposable circuit, interleaved OBDD and blocked OBDD.

A representation switch is structurally motivated only if the direct circuit stays linear while blocked OBDD grows materially faster; do not call the constructed separation representative of real workloads.
Report interleaved OBDD as a countercontrol showing that OBDD itself can remain compact under a favorable order.
No result is attributed to TiDiDi/TDD; direct circuit is an independent smooth deterministic decomposable prototype.
scope: Constructed independent-equivalence family only; exact rank-count semantics, not proof utility or TDD implementation performance.
